evals.prompt: Create a reusable React confirmation dialog for deleting a record. It should accept a title, description, pending state, confirm callback, and cancel callback, and it should work inside an existing TypeScript frontend with shared UI primitives.
evals.expected_output: A default-exported PascalCase function component with typed local props, explicit button types, accessible dialog semantics, a client directive only if required by the chosen dialog primitive, and an intentional pending state.
expectations: The component is declared as an exported default PascalCase function and has typed props.
The dialog and its controls have an accessible name, semantic action elements, and explicit button types.
Pending state prevents duplicate confirmation and communicates progress without breaking cancellation semantics.

evals.prompt: Refactor this feature screen into a page component and two feature modules: a filter bar and a results list. Keep the route server-rendered where possible, make only interactive code client-side, and add stable selectors for the filter input and result actions.
evals.expected_output: A feature-oriented component structure with default function declarations, a minimal client boundary, typed props, stable list keys, semantic markup, and selectors that are not tied to CSS classes or array indexes.
expectations: The screen is split into feature-oriented components with default function declarations and typed props.
Only interactive code uses a client boundary; the route/page remains server-compatible where possible.
Lists use stable domain keys and important controls use semantic or stable non-CSS selectors.
